import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/training_4.csv"
]

# Columns of the target table (and all source tables)
target_columns = ['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Module', 'Registered_Students']

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target columns (they are same per prompt)
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Since all source tables have the same schema as the target,
# we perform a UNION (concatenation) of all source tables.
# No transformation needed as columns match exactly.

# Concatenate all source DataFrames vertically
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Write the resulting DataFrame to the target CSV file
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_61/target_multisource_cot.csv", index=False)
